description:
Hello from Uruguay! 🇺🇾🚀

We are BMCY, a team of students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay, excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🌎✨
summary: Ares IX is a web-based strategy game created by Matías and Benjamín, two students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay. In the game, a space captain named Vance receives a mission: to build the first base on Mars. To succeed, the player must gather the resources needed to survive and build on the Red Planet. [Agregar: qué recursos y cómo se consiguen.] The game is inspired by one of NASA’s biggest real challenges: how humans will live on Mars using what they can find there instead of carrying everything from Earth. NASA has already tested this idea on Mars with MOXIE, a device that produced oxygen from the Martian air. Our game lets players experience this challenge themselves and think like the future engineers and astronauts who will build the first human outpost on Mars.
details:
What it does and how it works. The player takes the role of Captain Vance, who must complete a mission on Mars: building a base. To do this, the player must gather resources on the planet and use them to build and expand the base. [Agregar: controles, tipos de recursos, cómo se gana o se pierde.] The game runs in a web browser, so anyone can play it from a link without installing anything.

Benefits and intended impact. The game helps young people understand that living on Mars will require using local resources, and it encourages them to imagine solutions to real space-exploration problems.

Tools used. The game is published online with Netlify, and the presentation was made in Canva.

Creativity. Instead of a game about fighting or racing, we created a game about building and surviving, where the main challenge is planning how to use limited resources on another planet.

Factors we considered. What a base on Mars would really need, how to make gathering resources fun, and making the game easy to access online.
